paragraphs: Two Texts About One Morning, posted by Leo. Last Saturday, the Explorers joined an outdoor skills morning. It was a sunny day. It was in the nature park, and Ranger Mark taught us. Before the trip, we read a notice at the park gate. After the trip, I wrote a report. Here are both texts. Do they tell the same story?

Text One: The Park Notice. Join us for an Outdoor Skills Morning! Learn to tie a strong knot with a rope. Learn to read a map and find the way. The morning starts at nine o'clock and ends at eleven o'clock. It is free for children from ten to thirteen years old. Only twelve places are available.

Please ask Ranger Mark at the gate to keep a place for you. Bring a bottle of water and a hat, and wear strong shoes. You do not have to bring lunch. If it rains, we will meet in the park office. During the morning, you can chat with the rangers about birds and plants. Come and have fun!

Text Two: Leo's Report. Twelve children from our club came, and Tom and Ben helped us. First, Ranger Mark showed us a knot with a long rope. There was enough rope for everybody. I made a mistake, so Tom helped me. Ben tied the knot by himself, and it was very strong. When everyone was ready, we read a map and walked on the path to the lake. During the walk, we chatted with Ranger Mark about birds. It did not rain, and the morning ended at eleven o'clock. The lake was calm, and we sat on a big stone to eat a snack. At the end, we played a game with a list of five things to find. May found all five things easily, and she finished first.

Both texts give the same end time: eleven o'clock. Both texts tell about a knot and a map. Only the notice gives the number of places. Only my report tells about the game. Which text do you like more? Tell us in a message!
